# Fixed-normal cap transport: collision bounds and sharp parity loss

Let C be a compact convex body in R^n times R^d, n,d>=1, with actual
integer fibers K_z and positive total d-volume. Fix ONE nonzero ambient
linear functional f(z,x)=a.z+u.x. Define the closed-cap tails

    a_z(q)=|K_z intersect {f(z,x)>=q}|,
    G_r(q)=sum_(z congruent r mod 2) a_z(q),
    G(q)=sum_r G_r(q),
    Phi_d(A,B)=2^(-d)(A^(1/d)+B^(1/d))^d.

The finite transport theorem proved in
`candidate 87fbc7e80b2767d9` applies
directly to these traces. This note records a collision-resolved bound
and proves that its universal 2^n worst-case loss cannot be improved.
The examples retain one common ambient normal; they are not arbitrary
mixtures, independent normal minimizations, or depth counterexamples.

## 1. A computable collision-resolved cap bound

Fix s<=t and write h=(s+t)/2. For each parity r with G_r(t)>0, apply the
lexicographic consecutive-interval coupling to the two arrays of positive
trace volumes at s and t. Write its positive entries pi_(r,z,w); their
sum is one. The endpoints z,w have parity r, and their integer midpoint
k=(z+w)/2 is distinct for every positive entry within this parity path.

Let Phi_r=Phi_d(G_r(s),G_r(t)). At the corresponding target k define

    v_rk=pi_(r,z,w) Phi_r,
    c_rk=Phi_d(a_z(s),a_w(t)).

At unused targets set both quantities to zero. The proof of the finite
transport lemma gives c_rk>=v_rk. Actual convexity, with the SAME ambient
functional f, gives

    [K_z intersect {f>=s} + K_w intersect {f>=t}]/2
          subset K_k intersect {f>=h}.

Consequently the following exact lower bounds hold:

    G(h) >= sum_k max{a_k(t), max_r c_rk}
         >= sum_k max_r v_rk =: Q(s,t).                 (1)

The first term retains the actual monotone baseline a_k(t). The maximum
at a target, rather than a sum over its incoming parities, is essential.
Let p be the number of parities with G_r(t)>0 and put Omega=sum_r Phi_r.
When p>0,

    Q = Omega - sum_k [sum_r v_rk-max_r v_rk],
    max_r Phi_r <= Q <= Omega,
    Q >= Omega/p >= Omega/2^n.                          (2)

The bracket is the explicit loss from collisions at that target. If no
target occurs on two different parity paths, (1) retains the full Omega.
In general L_eff=Omega/Q lies between 1 and p and gives G(h)>=Omega/L_eff.
All of these quantities are determined by the finite cap-volume arrays
and the chosen translation-invariant lexicographic order. One may choose
another such order and retain the best bound. No joint disjointness of
the transported continuous sets is presumed.

Parities with G_r(t)=0 have no positive second array and are omitted from
Omega; applying the positive Phi formula to them would be invalid.
If a t-trace in that parity is nevertheless nonempty, even if null,
a fixed point in it can be paired with every positive s-trace. Distinct
source bases then have distinct midpoint targets and yield the separate
bound G(h)>=2^(-d) G_r(s). The same targetwise maximum convention applies
if such point-based contributions are added to (1). This includes
supporting traces and does not identify nonempty null sets with absent
sets. Vertical normals u=0 and their closed boundary mass are allowed.

## 2. The universal coefficient 2^(-n) is optimal

Even when EVERY parity has positive t-tail mass, no constant larger than
2^(-n) can replace it in

    G((s+t)/2) >= 2^(-n) sum_r Phi_d(G_r(s),G_r(t)).      (3)

This sharpness holds for actual full-dimensional simplices that equal
the convex hull of their actual mixed sets, and for the SAME genuinely
oblique functional f(z,x)=z_1+x_1 throughout the family.

For an integer N>=1 let

    C_N={z_i>=0, x_j>=0, sum_i z_i+2N sum_j x_j<=N}.

It is a full-dimensional simplex. All its vertices belong to the mixed
set: its nonzero base vertices have base coordinate N, while continuous
vertices have base zero. Hence C_N=conv(C_N intersect (Z^n times R^d)).
At integer z>=0, sum z<=N, the actual fiber is

    K_z=[(N-sum z)/(2N)] T_d,

where T_d is the standard d-simplex. The fibers with sum z<N are
positive, and the boundary fibers are points. On C_N, 0<=x_1<=1/2.
Therefore at every integer threshold q, the cap {z_1+x_1>=q} captures
exactly the full fibers z_1>=q and none of the others. The nonzero
continuous component of the ambient normal has not been dropped.

Write the unscaled cone mass as

    U_N=(1/d!) sum_(z in Z_+^n) (N-sum z)_+^d,
    D=n+d.

The elementary unit-cube comparison gives

    N^D/D! <= U_N <= (N+n)^D/D!.                        (4)

Indeed F_N(y)=(N-sum y)_+^d is coordinatewise decreasing. On the cube
z+[0,1]^n, F_N(y)<=F_N(z)<=F_(N+n)(y). Integrating the two outside
functions over R_+^n gives d! N^D/D! and d! (N+n)^D/D!, respectively.
This proves (4) without an unproved lattice asymptotic.

Set N=2L+n+1, L>=1, and choose s=0,t=2L,h=L. A translation of the
first base coordinate gives the EXACT identities

    G(0)=(2N)^(-d) U_(2L+n+1),
    G(L)=(2N)^(-d) U_(L+n+1),
    G(2L)=(2N)^(-d) U_(n+1).                            (5)

Every parity has positive G_r(2L): choose z_1=2L+r_1 and z_i=r_i for
i>1. Then sum z<=2L+n=N-1, so this fiber has positive volume and is in
the cap. Translation by 2L preserves parity, so after removing the
common factor (2N)^(-d), the t-tail parity masses are fixed positive
constants independent of L.

Let Omega_L=sum_r Phi_d(G_r(0),G_r(2L)). Since all second arguments are
positive, Omega_L>=2^(-d)G(0). Thus (4)-(5) give the explicit finite bound

    G(L)/Omega_L
       <= 2^d [(L+2n+1)/(2L+n+1)]^D
       = 2^(-n) [1+(3n+1)/(2L+n+1)]^D.                (6)

The lower bound (3) gives G(L)/Omega_L>=2^(-n). Formula (6) proves that
the ratio tends to exactly 2^(-n). It proves sharpness in every fixed
n,d, without replacing actual fibers by limiting measures.

For an explicit accuracy bound, if 0<epsilon<=1 and
L>=D(3n+1)/epsilon, the bracket in (6) has x=(3n+1)/(2L+n+1)
with Dx<=epsilon/2. The binomial expansion is bounded by
sum_(k>=0)(Dx)^k=1/(1-Dx)<=1+2Dx. Hence the ratio is at most
2^(-n)(1+epsilon). Any proposed larger universal coefficient therefore
fails for a finite integer L satisfying an explicit bound.

The collision-resolved quantity Q from (1) satisfies
Omega_L/2^n<=Q<=G(L). Therefore this SAME actual family also forces
Q/Omega_L to tend to 2^(-n), regardless of the chosen lexicographic
order. The sharp loss is not merely a defect of using a loose estimate
for one particular coupling. It is present in the actual target mass.

## 3. Aggregating the endpoint tails before Phi can fail arbitrarily badly

There is no positive constant c_d, even with n=1, such that every actual
source and every pair s<t satisfy

    G((s+t)/2) >= c_d Phi_d(G(s),G(t)).                  (7)

This is a different assertion from (3). The latter omits nonsurviving
parities before aggregation, which is necessary.

For A>=2 put two boxes at adjacent integer bases:

    K_0=[-2A-2,-A-2] times [0,1]^(d-1),
    K_1=[0,1]^d,
    C=conv(({0} times K_0) union ({1} times K_1)).

These are exactly the two integer fibers, of volumes A and 1, and C is
full dimensional. Again use the genuinely oblique f(z,x)=z+x_1. Take

    s=-2A-1, t=3/2, h=-A+1/4.

The s-cut is proper on K_0 and captures A-1 there plus the full K_1.
The t-cut is proper on K_1 and captures half of it, while missing K_0.
The midpoint cut lies in the gap between the two f-support intervals.
Consequently the exact tails are

    G(s)=A, G(t)=1/2, G(h)=1.

Since Phi_d(A,1/2)>A/2^d, the ratio in (7) is less than 2^d/A and tends
to zero. The nonsurviving parity is precisely the large first fiber.
Both selected endpoint cuts are proper, so this failure is not caused
by a convention about zero-volume supporting boundaries.

## 4. Scope and verification

Equations (1)-(2) are new finite lower bounds on the actual mass of ONE
fixed cap, with explicit collision information. Equation (3) is their
sharp dimension-only consequence; the cone family shows that the
factor cannot be improved without additional structural information.
Equation (7) is a separate, stronger and false root-concavity shortcut.
None of these statements selects a centroid, proves an ordinary or
mixed depth theorem, or places any center in a positive fiber.

The earlier `candidate 9af97e78b545b0b8` concerns
independent ordered endpoint sampling and simultaneous halfspace bounds
for a transported measure. Its sharp 2^n density example is different:
the present sharpness concerns actual fixed-normal target cap masses and
the collision-free lex paths. The forest load examples likewise do not
replace the finite cap-array argument above.

The exact companion verifier is
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_fixed_normal_cap_transport_sharp_parity_loss.py`.
